coverage.category: 32. Private educational and training institutions and nurseries (Law 4/2026; Child Law amendments)
coverage.found: Law 4/2026 in force 30 Jan 2026, with existing institutions to align by 30 Jan 2027. Nurseries: Child Law amendments criminalise unlicensed operation, a six-month grace period applies, and 110 licensed nurseries operate in 2025-26. Training institutes: still described by the Ministry of Labour page under Decree-Law 25/1998, plus ETQA listing within 6 months. Whether training institutes fall under Law 4 is unconfirmed. See C4, C5.

coverage.category: 33. Legal profession (new Legal Profession Law, 2026)
coverage.found: Reported Law 24/2026 of 14 June 2026 replacing Decree-Law 26/1980. Transition for lawyers and firms, mandatory professional indemnity insurance, separate professional bank accounts. The law number and the deadlines are unverified. See C8.

coverage.category: 34. Halal system and National Halal Mark (country-specific)
coverage.found: Decision 61/2024 and the 2026 mark resolution. Obligations fall on producers and certifying bodies; importers, restaurants and butchers are not mentioned in the source I read. See C1.

coverage.category: 35. MOIC commercial-registration and activity decisions (country-specific)
coverage.found: Resolution 43/2024 required one bank account per commercial entity by 13 June 2025 (passed). Edict 36/2026 lists commercial activities restricted to Bahrainis (list and deadline not seen). Resolution 36/2026 adds activities open to foreign-owned companies. Decisions 29/2024 and 53/2024 cover authorised distributors. See C14, C15.

coverage.category: 36. Supreme Council for Environment licences, waste and hazardous transport (country-specific)
coverage.found: Law 7/2022 on the environment. Hazardous waste transporter licence costs BHD 50 per vehicle. Waste management plan approval costs BHD 500. Fees under Ministerial Order 4/2021. Few buyers and a tiny market. See C11.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond what the searches showed. Bahrain has no small or private water systems of note: supply is a national grid run by EWA, so there are no village water boards, community schemes or small-utility operators to sell to. The only Bahrain-specific item found is a Ministry of Health service (Water Sample Certificate, Virtual Service Center) where EWA-approved contractors book inspection and water sampling of newly installed or maintained water pipes and storage tanks before connection to the public network. It is free, takes about 10 working days, and cites Public Health Law No. 34 of 2018. It is a one-off job-based step on the contractor side (needs a contractor letter and an EWA letter), not a recurring register, and it is state-run. I could not open the MOH page (HTTP 404), so this comes from the search snippet and is unverified in detail. No licensing rules were found for water tankers, bottled-water plants or Legionella and cooling-tower registration in Bahrain. Searches returned only UAE (Abu Dhabi tanker rules), Saudi and UK/Australia material. Whether such rules exist is unverified, not ruled out. Not pursued further because the market is small and grid-based.
